latest_release.name: SpotAPI 2.1.3 — Stability & Reliability Fixes
latest_release.body:
SpotAPI 2.1.3 improves reliability and fixes issues discovered during release verification.

- Fixed Spotify album decoding for object-shaped release timestamps.
- Fixed CLI authentication errors on systems without a supported keyring backend.
- Improved regression coverage and cross-platform reliability.
- Added automated release preflight checks to catch packaging issues before publication.

**Install or upgrade:**
`pip install -U spotapi`

detail.readme:
SpotAPI

Build Spotify apps in Python with a typed, async API.

Use SpotAPI for Spotify's public catalogue, playlists and connected players.
No developer app or API key for public data.

Get started · Explore · Python API · Documentation · Sponsor

Language: English · Português (Brasil) · Español · Français · 日本語

## Get started Python 3.11+ is required. Start with a real search—no Spotify login, Client ID or configuration needed. ```bash python -m pip install spotapi python -m spotapi search "Daft Punk" ``` Use the same API in Python: ```python import asyncio from spotapi import Public async def main(): results = await Public.search("Daft Punk", limit=5) for track in results.tracks: print(track.name, track.uri) asyncio.run(main()) ``` [More Python examples](#build-with-python) · [Playlist audit and CSV export](examples/playlist_audit.py) · [No-API-key Python guide](docs/no-api-key.md) The first request may be slower while SpotAPI discovers and caches the current web-player queries. Try the interactive terminal explorer: ```bash python -m pip install "spotapi[demo]" python -m spotapi discover "Daft Punk" ``` Navigate search results, artwork and Spotify links without signing in. [Discover example](https://github.com/Aran404/SpotAPI/blob/main/examples/discover.py) · [Troubleshooting](https://the-open-odyssey.pages.dev/docs/spotapi/troubleshooting/) ## Explore in the terminal The CLI goes beyond search. Inspect an artist, pull track credits, or list a public playlist: ```bash python -m spotapi search "Daft Punk" --type artist --json python -m spotapi get SPOTIFY_URL python -m spotapi playlist items PLAYLIST_ID --limit 10 ``` These work without a developer API key. Account operations—liked music, private playlists and control of your existing Spotify player—require your own Spotify session. See the [account guide](https://the-open-odyssey.pages.dev/docs/spotapi/account/) and [player guide](https://the-open-odyssey.pages.dev/docs/spotapi/player/). ### Connect: control your Spotify player Connect brings searching, device selection, up-next, playback and a live activity log into one keyboard-friendly terminal session. It operates an existing signed-in Spotify player; it does **not** stream, download or decrypt tracks. ![SpotAPI Connect controlling a real Spotify player from the terminal](assets/cli-connect-demo.gif)

Connect · Search, navigate and control an existing Spotify player from your terminal. Spotify plays the audio; SpotAPI sends the controls.

Launch Connect: ```bash python -m pip install "spotapi[connect,browser]" python -m playwright install chromium python -m spotapi connect ``` First-time browser sign-in is covered by these commands. Already use `SPOTIFY_COOKIE` or a saved Connect profile? Install only `spotapi[connect]` and skip the browser download. Use `search Daft Punk`, `queue 1`, `pause`, `next` or `seek 1:30`. `Ctrl+P` opens the command palette. See the [Connect guide](docs/connect.md) for device selection and setup. ## See what else it can do SpotAPI also powers **Studio**, a desktop music explorer built on the same library. Open tracks, inspect credits, follow artists and albums, and display timed lyrics. With a connected Spotify player, clicking a lyric can seek playback to that line. ![SpotAPI Studio desktop application preview](examples/studio/preview.png) [Watch the synchronized-lyrics demo (GIF, about 11 MB)](assets/lyrics-sync-demo.gif) · Studio itself does not stream full Spotify tracks. ```bash python -m pip install "spotapi[studio]" python -m spotapi studio ``` Studio uses a native WebView. [Studio setup](https://the-open-odyssey.pages.dev/docs/spotapi/studio/) explains platform requirements and Spotify sign-in. Lyric availability depends on the source and account entitlements; seeking needs an authenticated, controllable player. ## Support SpotAPI Sponsors help keep SpotAPI free and fund maintenance, testing and documentation. [Become a sponsor](SPONSORSHIP.md).

## Build with Python Reuse a catalogue session for related operations: ```python import asyncio from spotapi import Catalogue async def main() -> None: async with Catalogue() as spotify: results = await spotify.search("Daft Punk") if results.artists: artist = await spotify.get_artist(results.artists[0].uri) print(artist.name) asyncio.run(main()) ``` **Working with large playlists?** [Audit up to 10,000 playlist occurrences](examples/playlist_audit.py), identify duplicate tracks and unavailable entries, and export a CSV. The example pages through results instead of loading the whole playlist into memory. Run it from a repository checkout. ### Where to go next | Build | Start here | |---|---| | Music search or public metadata tools | [Public catalogue](https://the-open-odyssey.pages.dev/docs/spotapi/catalogue/) | | A playlist organizer that handles duplicate tracks correctly | [Playlist API](https://the-open-odyssey.pages.dev/docs/spotapi/account/) | | A live now-playing display or controller | [Player example](https://github.com/Aran404/SpotAPI/blob/main/examples/player.py) | | A personal music dashboard | [Account and statistics](https://the-open-odyssey.pages.dev/docs/spotapi/account/) | | A DJ crate using tempo and harmonic keys | [Playlist crate](https://github.com/Aran404/SpotAPI/blob/main/examples/playlist_crate.py) | | An experimental local music recommender | [Taste Lab](https://github.com/Aran404/SpotAPI/blob/main/examples/taste_lab/README.md) | ## Why SpotAPI? - **Start without credentials.** Public catalogue search and metadata require no Spotify developer app. - **Typed, async results.** Work with Python models instead of guessing dictionary keys. - **Explicit I/O.** Reading a model doesn't silently trigger another HTTP request. - **More than read-only metadata.** With your authenticated session, manage saved music, edit playlist occurrences and control existing players. - **Designed for exploration.** Use the CLI, Discover and Studio to understand capabilities before integrating them into code. SpotAPI uses unofficial Spotify web-player endpoints, so behavior can change when Spotify changes those endpoints. It is **not** a substitute for the official Web API in every use case, and public-data access is different from authenticated playback access. [Compare the APIs](https://the-open-odyssey.pages.dev/docs/spotapi/from-spotipy/) · [Verification boundaries](https://the-open-odyssey.pages.dev/docs/spotapi/release-checks/#boundaries) ## Documentation and migration [Quickstart](https://the-open-odyssey.pages.dev/docs/spotapi/quickstart/) · [API reference](https://the-open-odyssey.pages.dev/docs/spotapi/reference/) · [Coming from Spotipy](https://the-open-odyssey.pages.dev/docs/spotapi/from-spotipy/) · [CLI and discovery](https://the-open-odyssey.pages.dev/docs/spotapi/discovery/) · [Troubleshooting](https://the-open-odyssey.pages.dev/docs/spotapi/troubleshooting/) **Upgrading from v1?** SpotAPI 2 is async-first and contains breaking changes. Existing v1 apps can pin `spotapi==1.2.8` while migrating, or use `SyncCatalogue` for new synchronous scripts. Read the [migration guide](MIGRATION.md). ## Contributing Bug reports, reproducible issues and thoughtful contributions are welcome. [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [Tests](tests/README.md) · [Legal notice](LEGAL_NOTICE.md) · [GPL-3.0](LICENSE) If SpotAPI helps you build something, **[star the repository](https://github.com/Aran404/SpotAPI)** to help other developers discover it.
